notes: GeoTalk 1.14: the battery-permission button now actually takes you to the switch. On TECNO and Infinix phones the standard battery prompt sometimes never appears, so the 'Battery use' Allow button in Profile led nowhere — now, if the battery is still restricted after one Allow tap, the button opens GeoTalk's own App info page instead, where the switch is one tap deeper (Battery → Unrestricted), and the checklist spells out those exact taps. The app also asks again on the first open after this update if anything is still missing, so updating is the moment to finish the one-time setup. And the built-in call listener is steadier with the screen off: each of its checks now briefly holds the phone awake until the check has finished, so a call check that starts also completes instead of being frozen half-way by the sleeping phone. Everything from 1.13 is kept in full: incoming calls now use Android's real calling presentation. When the phone's screen is off, a call opens full-screen over the lock screen with the caller's name and Answer/Decline; when you are busy in another app or watching a video, the same call appears in the notification bar with working Answer and Decline buttons. A one-time setup makes this fully reliable on TECNO and Infinix phones: on first open the app asks for the few system switches it cannot turn on by itself (full-screen calls, unrestricted battery use, notifications), each with a button that opens the exact settings page — and the same checklist stays in Profile under 'Call readiness' if you ever need it again. Answering from a notification is also fixed for when the app was completely closed: the tap is now followed through until the call is on screen and answered, instead of getting lost while the app starts up. And the built-in call listener now restarts itself if the system or a swipe from recents removes it, so calls keep arriving while the app is closed. Everything from 1.12 is kept in full: answer or decline a call right from its notification, see on the call screen whether the other phone is really ringing, and connect faster after answering. NOTIFICATION ACTIONS — an incoming call's notification now has Answer and Decline buttons: tap Answer to pick the call up without opening the app first, or Decline to cut it right from the notification. CALLING / RINGING — the outgoing call screen now shows what is really happening: Calling... while the other phone has not rung yet (it may be offline, or its app may be closed), and Ringing... as soon as the other phone actually rings. FASTER AFTER ANSWER — while an answered call is connecting, the app now re-checks the voice-confirmation signal instead of sending it only once, so a single lost signal can no longer leave the call sitting on Connecting... — answered calls reach live voice faster. Everything from 1.11 is kept in full: incoming calls now ring with the full call screen even when the app is closed, and calls connect noticeably faster. APP-CLOSED CALLS — a small built-in listener stays ready after you open the app once: it watches for calls addressed to you and rings with the usual ringtone and the full call screen even if GeoTalk is closed (a quiet notification shows it is on; for best results allow GeoTalk unrestricted battery use in system settings; you can turn it off any time in Profile — 'Incoming calls when app is closed'). No account or server setup is needed for this. FASTER CONNECTS — the connection path is now prepared while the phone is still ringing: both phones publish their connection addresses at the start of the call and keep the path warm with tiny test pings, so when a call is answered the direct engine starts on an already-open path and voice begins in about a second or two instead of several seconds of connecting first. Everything from 1.10 is kept in full: calls have to prove they carry real sound — if the first connection path connects but no voice has arrived within about eight seconds, the app automatically switches the call to the proven direct engine instead of staying silent, and a path that connected without carrying voice no longer counts as the remembered good path (the app remembers the path that actually carried your voice); every internet call records its voice-packet counts (received and sent) into the problem report, whichever engine carried it; the one-way-audio fixes for direct calls (connection addresses refreshed at the moment a call connects, the voice path chosen and held by real voice rather than test pings, looped-back copies of your own voice recognised and dropped, direct local path when both phones share one connection); call-back by tapping any entry in the Calls tab (incoming, outgoing or missed); the complete 1.7 feature set with the 1.7 launch problem fixed — push starts safely after the app opens and can never block or break it, faster calls via the remembered proven path and ringing-time connection preparation, Opus HD voice (wideband 16 kHz, adaptive about 16–40 kbps with error correction) that stays clear on slow connections at roughly a tenth of the data, push incoming calls with the full call screen even when the app is closed (this activates as soon as the push service is switched on for your account — no app update will be needed after that), the independent direct-UDP live voice engine between WebRTC and Push-to-Talk, native crash details in problem reports, the call safety guard that resets on every new version, call signaling on its own dedicated thread, proper telephony audio mode with audio focus, incoming calls ring with your default ringtone and vibration, direct phone-to-phone WebRTC voice first, Cloudflare TURN relay (UDP, TCP and TLS 443) when a network blocks the direct path, Push-to-Talk as the final fallback, plus internet and Bluetooth chat + voice calls, voice messages and in-app updates.
